newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-NEWCASTLE UNDER SCRUTINY AFTER KEEGAN'S DEPARTURE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NEWCASTLE UNDER SCRUTINY AFTER KEEGAN'S DEPARTURE.

text.p: Newcastle United enter an uncertain era when they play Aston Villa in an English premier league match at Villa Park on Saturday without the inspirational Kevin Keegan in the dug-out.
Keegan quit as manager on Wednesday in the biggest shock of the season so far.

His departure made headlines on both the front and back pages of newspapers and it will be a huge test of Newcastle's character and real title potential when they meet Brian Little's side, beaten only once in their last eight matches but looking for their first win in four.

Newcastle assistant manager Terry McDermott and wily old veteran manager Arthur Cox will be in charge on Saturday while the club continues the hunt for Keegan's replacement. Peter Beardsley is reported to be the fans favourite, while the Newcastle board are said to be wooing John Toshack and Kenny Dalglish among others after former England coach Bobby Robson formally turned the job down on Friday.

But it is not inconceivable that if McDermott and Cox can string a good run together while negotiations continue they could keep control of the team at least until the end of the season, if not longer.
Keegan stunned the world of soccer this week with the timing of his resignation, although the fact he might be quitting had been rumoured for some time.

His most telling remark about why he went was because he felt he had taken Newcastle as far down the road to success as he could. That is a staggering admission for a soccer manager to have made after spending 60 million pounds ($100 million) in building his side, and it will be absorbing to see just how far Newcastle now go in capturing the honours he failed to bring them.

It is unlikely there will be anything dramatically different about Newcastle's team or tactics on Saturday. French winger David Ginola should return to the side after a calf injury but Colombian Faustino Asprilla remains sidelined with a hamstring. Northern Ireland striker Keith Gillespie is back in contention after recovering from influenza.

Newcastle go to Villa Park fourth in the table and still with every chance of the title. They have won their last two league matches with a goal tally of 10-1 and face a Villa side two places below them.

The last time Newcastle played a match without Keegan as manager was on February 1, 1992 when they crashed 5-2 at Oxford United to leave themselves one from bottom in the old second division and favourites for relegation to the old division three. Keegan took over four days later, and the rest, as they say, is history.

The fact that now, without Keegan, they are just five points off the pace in the title race with a game in hand, in the quarter-finals of the UEFA Cup and also still in the F.A. Cup, is indication enough of just far how along the road they travelled under his stewardship.

Soccer is eagerly awaiting Saturday's match to look for Newcastle's reaction, to see whether Keegan's departure will end their title challenge -- or galvanise them into a side capable of winning silverware without him.
